div.note: Liebermann's text is from H (Textus Roffensis f. 32, after Forfang 1, in the same hand, c. 1120), the same manuscript as the modern edition. The heading is in red. Since clause 1 begins with ‘And’, the beginning is lacking, and the heading, which presents this fragment of a royal law as an independent work, is therefore not original. Liebermann dates it c. 936–58 or up to c. 1000. In the Quadripartitus it follows VI As. Clause number standardised from ‘Ord. Inscr.’.; U: added from Attenborough p. 171, October 2026 (the modern editor’s translation); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.936–58, or c.1000; ?c. 930 (Wormald)”, now “c.936–58 or –c.1000 (Liebermann); ?c.930 (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.936–58 or –c.1000 (Liebermann); ?c.930 (Wormald)”, now “c.936–58 or –c.1000 (Liebermann, I p. 386); ?c.930 (Wormald, MEL pp. 373–4)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “H 386; Q 386; German 386”; 13 rows of Ordal)

note.seg: Die Überschrift kann nicht original sein, da Einzelkapitel in Gesetzen 10. Jhs. keine Überschriften tragen. Aus den in H und Q stehenden verrät sich kaum ein identisches Wort; dom hätte Q wohl durch iudicium wiedergegeben, während constitutio (institutum) in Q-Lond eher gerædnes entspricht. Die Rubren, die sich nur in Q's jüngster Rezension finden, pflegen deren eignes Werk zu sein. Es bleibt also fraglich, ob der Archetyp hq Be ordale überschrieb oder wie H las. In letzterem Falle müsste H haten aus hatum abgeschwächt haben

The heading cannot be original, since individual chapters in laws of the 10th cent. bear no headings. Between the headings in H and Q scarcely a single word can be seen to be identical; Q would probably have rendered dom by iudicium, whereas constitutio (institutum) in Q-Lond corresponds rather to gerædnes. The rubrics found only in Q's latest recension are usually its own work. It therefore remains doubtful whether the archetype hq bore the heading Be ordale or read as H does. In the latter case H would have had to weaken hatum to haten

Das Wort dom braucht H in den Überschriften oft für ‘Gesetz’. Auch hier ist diese Bed. wahrscheinlich. Denn zur anderen (s. Wb 5) stände wohl Wasser und Eisen im Genetiv wie wæteres dom Iud Dei VIII 2

H often uses the word dom in its headings for ‘law’. This meaning is probable here too. For with the other meaning (see Wb 5) water and iron would probably stand in the genitive, as in wæteres dom Iud Dei VIII 2
Für Kesselfang und Glüheisen lautet das Ritual oft identisch; s. Gl Feuerordal 1. 7
The ritual for the cauldron ordeal and for the red-hot iron is often identically worded; see Gl Feuerordal 1. 7
